subject: Dedicated capacity questions — Orbitex RFP & compute orchestration
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@orbitex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitex.com
Date: 2028-01-18T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Orbitex RFP: committed throughput targets and burst profile

Neha / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We're targeting a production launch in Q2 and want a committed dedicated footprint that meets our SLOs while keeping unit costs predictable. High-level traffic: 12M tokens/day sustained, with diurnal peak ~2.5x at 16:00-18:00 PST and 5-minute microbursts up to 6x sustained rate. Average request size: 350 tokens, tail requests (e.g., long-form generation) 1–2% at ~2,000 tokens.

SLOs: p95 latency <= 500ms for interactive calls (our default model, 8k context quantized variant), p99 <= 1.5s. We also need a canary strategy for first 72 hours and a fallback path if capacity is saturated.

Attached is the RFP and our traffic extract. Can you confirm an initial dedicated slab recommendation (GPU count / type), expected tokens/sec throughput, and suggested safety buffer? Also list any operational constraints (cold starts, cache warmup).

Regards,
Amit Shah
Head of Platform, Orbitex

Attachment: Orbitex_RFP_Q1.pdf (pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@orbitex.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-18T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbitex RFP: committed throughput targets and burst profile

Amit — thanks, got the RFP. Looping in Karthik and Ben to run a capacity sketch. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we do full math:

- Which model variant do you expect to serve in the committed slab? (you mentioned 8k context quantized)
- Are the 6x microbursts short-lived (seconds) or sustained for multiple minutes?
- Do you plan to enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (helpful for lower token cost)?

High level, we can give: a tokens/sec recommendation, p95 fit, and an ops playbook (canary + cache warmup). We'll follow up with a short calc and two options: cost-optimized (smaller slab + aggressive caching) and SLO-first (larger slab + burst buffer).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

---
Neha Kapoor
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Amit Shah <amit@orbitex.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Orbitex RFP: compute sketch and tokens/sec math

All — did a first-pass model and attached a spreadsheet (compute_estimate_v1.xlsx). Key assumptions and numbers below. If Amit confirms the 8k quantized variant and the microbursts are ~3–5 minutes, these numbers hold.

Assumptions:
- Model: open-8k-quant (8k context, int8 quantized)
- Avg tokens per request: 350
- Sustained tokens/day: 12,000,000 -> avg tokens/sec sustained = 12,000,000 / (24*3600) ≈ 138.9 t/s
- Diurnal peak multiplier: 2.5x -> peak sustained ~347.2 t/s
- Microburst multiplier: 6x -> burst short windows ~833 t/s
- P95 latency target: 500ms (includes network + infra; we budget 350ms server-side)

Server throughput baseline (per GPU):
- H100 (quantized run): ~1500 t/s (single model shard, continuous batching, warm KV cache)
- A100 (quantized run): ~850 t/s

Capacity sketches:
1) SLO-first slab (low latency margin):
- Active GPUs: 1 H100 equivalent handles ~1500 t/s, so sustained peak 347 t/s comfortably fits on a single GPU with headroom, but microbursts (833 t/s) need headroom -> recommend 2 H100 equivalents (redundancy + warm cache).
- Suggested slab: 2x H100 (dedicated), configured with automatic horizontal burst to spare capacity in regionally nearby pool if needed.
- Headroom: ~80% free for microburst absorption and canary traffic.
- Expected p95 server-side latency: ~280–360ms under sustained peak, p99 ~700–900ms under 6x microburst without fallback.

2) Cost-optimized slab:
- 1 H100 equivalent + aggressive prefix caching and request shaping -> handles sustained peak with careful rate limiting, but microbursts will trigger graceful degradation (retries + fallback to a smaller model).
- Add an on-call surge pool (shared reserved capacity) for 3x short bursts.

Additional operational notes:
- KV/prefix cache warmup: first 30–45 minutes of traffic reduce token cost by ~10–20% for repeated prompts; recommend canary warmup for 24–48 hours ahead of full launch.
- Cold-start: model cold-start time ~8–12s for a fully evicted Quant model on our runtime; we recommend pinning critical routes or keeping model hot in the slab.
- Canary: route 1% traffic for 72 hours then 10% for 24 hours before ramping to 100%. Monitor tokens/sec and p95 latency on the route.

I'll iterate with Ben on cost math (commit vs burst pricing). Karthik

Attachment: compute_estimate_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@orbitex.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-19T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbitex RFP: cost / SLA tradeoffs and burst strategy

Amit — quick follow-up on the economics and SLA guardrails. Two concrete recommendations to balance cost and reliability:

1) Commit tier + burst credits: recommend a 2x H100-equivalent reserved slab for guaranteed latency (SLO-first). Offer a 20% monthly burst credit pool (pre-purchased token buffer) that Orbitex can consume for occasional >6x peaks. That keeps the committed price predictable while covering rare events.

2) Fallback policy: configure automatic model fallback to a 4k quantized variant when server-side p95 exceeds 600ms for more than 90s. That keeps user-facing latency within p99 targets. Documented rollback: immediate route weight reduction + notify Orbitex ops.

Cost ballpark (monthly):
- 2x H100 reserved: $XXXk/mo (exact number in attached sheet with amortized infra ops)
- 1x H100 + burst credits: ~0.6x cost of SLO-first but higher risk of degraded latency during long microbursts.

Operational checklist (for the contract):
- SLA: p95 <= 500ms for interactive routes, with credits for any monthly retrogression.
- Canary runbook included in onboarding SOW.

If this looks good, we can surface a term sheet and draft the commitment schedule.

-ben

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@orbitex.com>, procurement@orbitex.com
Date: 2028-01-20T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbitex RFP: committed throughput targets and burst profile

Thanks, team. This is very helpful. Confirming Orbitex preference for the SLO-first option (2x H100-equivalent) with the 20% monthly burst credit. We also want the fallback to 4k quantized variant and the 72-hour canary.

Next steps from procurement: please send an itemized term sheet and the canary runbook appendix so we can review legal and our infra team can map networking. Also please include the expected p95 and p99 numbers based on Karthik's sketch in the term sheet.

Elena Rossi
VP, Platform Engineering — Orbitex
